title: A Single Cell Shrinks to 1/4 Its Length in 5 Milliseconds

scenes.text: A single cell shrinks to a quarter of its length in milliseconds.
It is a giant pond creature made of just one cell.
It squeezes down in under five milliseconds.
That is hundreds of times faster than a blink.
It moves about one hundred body lengths every second.
Human muscle can shorten that much too, but it takes about ten times longer.
Its trigger is calcium, not the fuel our muscles use. One cell, faster than you.

description:
A single cell shrinks to a quarter of its length in milliseconds.
The pond creature Spirostomum ambiguum contracts in under five milliseconds, hundreds of times faster than a blink, and calcium appears to power it.
What is the fastest thing you have ever seen?
first_comment: Bonus: its engine is a web of proteins that tighten when calcium arrives, a bit like a fishnet pulled shut. What else would you like to see in slow motion?
